description: We are Andes Space Systems, a team developing ARES-Health, an autonomous health monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration space missions. Our goal is to combine electronics, programming, biomedical sensors, and data analysis to help astronauts monitor their health and respond to potential risks. We welcome passionate people interested in aerospace, software development, biomedical engineering, AI, and data visualization.
summary: ARES-Health is an autonomous, edge-computing medical software platform designed for deep space missions where communication delays with Earth make real-time telemedicine impossible. The system continuously monitors crew vital signs using wearable sensors—tracking metrics like heart rate, SpO2, temperature, and muscle activity—while integrating space weather data via the NASA DONKI API. It processes this telemetry locally to evaluate the astronaut's well-being through a custom Space Risk Index (SRI). If physiological anomalies, fatigue, or critical risks are detected, the system instantly provides step-by-step clinical countermeasures without relying on ground control connectivity. This project addresses the critical challenge of deep-space medical autonomy, ensuring crew safety, preventing physiological deterioration, and bridging the gap between terrestrial healthcare and planetary exploration.
details:
What it does & How it works:

ARES-Health is an astronaut health monitoring and telemetry software platform developed for Andes Space Systems. It operates via a robust Python/FastAPI backend utilizing real-time WebSockets (at 50 Hz) to stream biomedical data—such as ECG waveforms, heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature, and EMG muscle activity—paired with a responsive HTML/Tailwind CSS/Chart.js frontend featuring dual-view interfaces for both the local astronaut HUD and Earth Mission Control.

Benefits & Expected Impact: The project ensures crew safety and operational autonomy during long-duration deep space transit (such as missions to Mars). By handling communication blackouts locally and calculating a multi-variable Space Risk Index (SRI), it prevents false alarms, distinguishes between normal exercise and physiological anomalies, and provides immediate local medical guidance without waiting for ground control.

Ts, Languages, & Technologies Used: Developed using Python, FastAPI, WebSockets, HTML5, Tailwind CSS, Chart.js, and asynchronous event loops. It integrates official NASA data sources including the NASA DONKI API for real-time solar radiation and space weather, NASA OSDR datasets, and NASA-STD-3001 clinical standards.

Creativity & Factors Considered: ARES-Health stands out by solving a critical space engineering challenge: communication latency and blackouts. The team carefully considered modular architecture, explainable AI/analytics for risk evaluation, local data buffering, and fault-tolerant synchronization between the spacecraft and Earth Mission Control.ool
